sections.heading: A giant lattice of ions
sections.text:
An ionic compound is not made of separate molecules. Millions of positive and negative ions are packed in a regular three-dimensional pattern called a giant ionic lattice.
Every ion is attracted strongly by the oppositely charged ions around it. These strong forces explain the properties.

sections.heading: High melting points, brittle crystals
sections.text:
Melting means freeing the ions, which needs a lot of energy: salt melts at about {801} °C, magnesium oxide at about {2800} °C.
Ionic compounds are hard crystals, but brittle: a sharp blow shifts the layers so that ions of the same charge meet, they repel, and the crystal shatters.

sections.heading: Dissolving and conducting
sections.text:
Many ionic compounds dissolve in water, because water molecules attract the ions and pull them apart; they do not dissolve in kerosene or petrol.
To conduct electricity, charged particles must move. In the solid the ions are fixed, so it does not conduct. Molten or dissolved, the ions move freely, so it conducts.

key_words.meaning: a huge regular arrangement of ions
a molten or dissolved ionic compound that conducts

examples: NaCl: m.p. {801} °C, soluble, conducts in solution
MgO: very high m.p., used to line furnaces

mistake.wrong: Solid salt conducts because it contains ions
mistake.right: Solid salt does not conduct: its ions cannot move
mistake.why: Ions must be free to move to carry a current.

worked_example.problem: Explain why solid salt does not conduct electricity but salt water does.
steps: Electricity needs charged particles that can move.
In solid salt the ions are held in fixed positions in the lattice.
When salt dissolves, the ions separate and move freely, so the solution conducts.
worked_example.answer: The ions can move only when dissolved (or molten)

cards.idea: Strong forces between ions: high melting points.
Ionic compounds conduct only when molten or dissolved.
example: The ions must be free to move.

cards.idea: Many ionic compounds dissolve in water, not in kerosene.
example: Salt dissolves in water; it does not dissolve in kerosene.

pick.q: Common salt is mixed with kerosene. What happens?
e: Ionic compounds dissolve in water, not organic solvents.
pick.y: Ionic compounds are generally insoluble in organic solvents.

pick.q: Which property is typical of an ionic compound?
e: Ionic compounds have high boiling points.
Solid ionic compounds do not conduct.
pick.y: Shifting the layers brings like charges together, so the crystal splits.

pick.q: Why do many ionic compounds dissolve in water?
pick.r: Water molecules attract and separate the ions
pick.y: The ions spread out among the water molecules.

pick.q: Why does sodium chloride have a high melting point?
pick.r: Strong forces hold the ions together in a giant lattice
w: It contains a metal that is hard to melt
e: It has no separate molecules; it is a lattice of ions.
It is the ionic bonding, not the metal, that matters.
Weak forces would give a low melting point.
pick.y: Much energy is needed to break the many strong ionic bonds.

pick.q: At room temperature, ionic compounds are usually…
pick.y: High melting points: solid at room temperature.

pick.q: Which has the highest melting point?
pick.y: Ionic lattices have high melting points.

pick.q: When does an ionic compound conduct electricity?
pick.r: when molten or dissolved in water
e: In the solid the ions cannot move.
It does conduct when the ions are free.

pick.q: What carries the current in molten sodium chloride?
e: Free electrons carry current in metals.
There is no water in the melt.
pick.y: In ionic liquids, ions carry the current.

pick.q: Why does solid potassium chloride not conduct electricity?
pick.r: Its ions are fixed in place
e: Free electrons would make it conduct.
pick.y: Charged particles must move to carry current.

pick.q: A white solid melts at 770 °C, dissolves in water, and its solution conducts electricity. What type of substance is it?
e: Simple covalent substances have low melting points and do not conduct.
Metals conduct as solids and do not dissolve in water.
pick.y: High melting point, soluble, conducts in solution: ionic.

pick.q: Which result shows a substance is NOT ionic?
e: Many ionic compounds dissolve in water.
pick.y: A low melting point means weak forces: not ionic.

pick.q: A compound conducts when molten but not when solid. Its bonding is…
e: Covalent compounds do not conduct when molten.
pick.y: Ions become free to move when it melts.
